newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uranium-rich Kazakhstan sets up atomic energy firm.
newsitem.headline: Uranium-rich Kazakhstan sets up atomic energy firm.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev has signed a decree creating a national state-run atomic energy company, the official Khabar news programme said on Tuesday.
The new company, to be called Kazatomprom, would include KATEP, the state-owned Company on Atomic Power Engineering and Industry.

"We plan to increase the production of uranium and ensure a larger degree of its processing," KATEP head Viktor Yazikov said, commenting on the decree. He said Kazatomprom would also comprise three uranium mines, a geological company and the Ulbinsky metallurgical plant.
"This branch (of the economy) is being made more orderly," Yazikov said, adding Kazatomprom would mean stronger state control over the production and export of uranium.
Kazakhstan, which holds a quarter of the world's reserves of uranium ores, produces 1,240 tonnes of uranium a year, compared to 3,200 tonnes in Soviet days, Yazikov said.
He said Kazakhstan currently ranks seventh among the world's exporters of uranium but declined to provide any concrete data.
The former Soviet republic's uranium exports include concentrate of uranium oxide-protoxide to the United States as well as fuel for atomic power stations in Russia, Ukraine and Bulgaria.
"Kazakhstan does not export enriched uranium because it lacks plants for its production," Yazikov said, adding the Central Asian state planned to produce fuel for Western power stations as well.
Kazakhstan -- a vast steppeland country five times the size of France -- has five atomic reactors.
Safety controls over the atomic industry would rest with the National Atomic Agency, Yazikov said.
